Subject: Clarify small-volume floor for microbursts + KV cache crediting

Hi Neha,

Quick question as we finalize the pilot SOW: our product produces frequent short inference spikes (50–200 tokens each, recurring every few minutes). On the invoices I saw a 1,000-token minimum per session — can you confirm whether those microbursts will be aggregated into a single session for billing, or treated separately (which would trigger the minimum multiple times)?

Separately, we noticed that some of the requests hit identical prefixes that should use KV cache re-use. Is Redwood applying any prefix/KV cache crediting that reduces billable token counts for repeated prefixes within a billing window? If so, how would that interplay with the session minimum?

I've attached a redacted sample invoice and a short log excerpt to show burst patterns. We need to understand this before procurement signs off.

Can we get a short written example showing the worst-case and best-case billable tokens for a 24-hour window? Also, if there's a short-term waiver path for low-volume pilots, please flag that — Acme wants to proceed but needs a predictable floor.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor

Hi Liam — following up with the billing examples. TL;DR: microbursts are billed per request unless they are part of the same open session and share KV cache state; KV cache reuse reduces compute tokens billed, but the session minimum still applies per session instance. That said, there are two levers we can use for pilots: 1) group short-lived calls into a short-lived session (SDK change) to avoid repeated minimums, or 2) grant a temporary pilot floor waiver/credit (commercial).

Worked examples (simplified):

Scenario A — No session aggregation: 1,000 microbursts, each 150 tokens, no KV reuse
- Billable tokens per burst: max(150, session_minimum=1,000) => 1,000
- Total billed tokens = 1,000 bursts * 1,000 tokens = 1,000,000 tokens

Scenario B — Session aggregation (server keeps one session open for bursts), no KV reuse
- All bursts within same session: session billed once at max(total_session_tokens, session_minimum)
- If cumulative tokens across bursts = 150,000 -> billed tokens = max(150,000, 1,000) = 150,000

Scenario C — Session aggregation + KV reuse (50% of bursts hit cached prefixes and save 80% compute tokens)
- Effective compute tokens after KV crediting = 150,000 * (1 - 0.5 * 0.8) = 150,000 * 0.6 = 90,000
- Billed tokens = max(90,000, 1,000) = 90,000

Notes:
- The "KV crediting" above is effectively a reduction applied to billable compute tokens when a prefix reuse is detected in the same session/window. It does not reduce the session minimum below the stated floor.
- For very small pilots where SDK changes are impractical, we can offer a temporary billing credit that effectively reduces the calculated billed tokens on invoices (one-off credit line) while you validate product fit.

Attached a tiny workbook with these calculations you can tweak (kv_cache_credit_examples.xlsx). Vanessa, can you confirm the standard pilot credit level we can offer (percent / token cap)?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Pricing Solutions, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Clarify small-volume floor for microbursts + KV cache crediting

Thanks Jordan — that helped a lot and the worked numbers make the tradeoffs clear. Two follow-ups:

1) For the pilot, would Redwood be willing to apply a 90% cap credit on session-minimum overage for the first 30 days (essentially limit the per-session billable floor to 100 tokens for pilot invoices)? We can commit to a 3-month evaluation if the pilot metrics meet our latency/cost targets.
2) If we keep a single open session via the SDK, are there any limits to session duration (we want to keep it open across many small bursts for 24–72 hours)? Any server-side TTLs we should be aware of?

If you can confirm the waiver path and TTL limits by end of week, procurement will proceed to sign the pilot SOW.

Appreciate the quick turn — Liam
